adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql_command.go, the go-duck import is removed but the code now calls sql.NewInMemoryDB() (and uses sql.*). The import block shown in the diff does not add an import for the new pkg/expr/sql package (or any sql package), so the identifier `sql` will be undefined and the file will not compile.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TablesList in parser.go always fails because duckDB.RunCommands is a stub, breaking table name extraction and reference resolution for {{refId}} references

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, TablesList now calls NewInMemoryDB() (local) instead of duck.NewInMemoryDB(). The new DB implementation in pkg/expr/sql/db.go has RunCommands() stubbed to always return an error ("not implemented"), so TablesList's call to duckDB.RunCommands(...) will always fail, breaking table-name extraction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error message 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' at reader.go:130-131 is misleading since it actually indicates a feature-flag disabled condition

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/expr/reader.go`, the SQL branch returns `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` when `enableSqlExpressions(h)` is false (new guard at ~126-131). `enableSqlExpressions` bases its decision on the feature flag (`h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`), so this error is at least tied to feature-flag gating rather than purely “not implemented”. That makes the message potentially misleading to callers about why SQL expressions are rejected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: enableSqlExpressions always returns false due to contradictory dead logic, making the FlagSqlExpressions feature flag non-functional and causing all QueryTypeSQL requests to fail unconditionally

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, enableSqlExpressions() contains dead/contradictory logic: it sets `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns `false` both inside the `if enabled { ... }` block and at the end, so it always returns false. In ReadQuery() for QueryTypeSQL, this causes `if !enabled { return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented") }` to trigger unconditionally, making all QueryTypeSQL reads fail regardless of the FlagSqlExpressions setting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL is built by string interpolation in TablesList with only single-quote doubling as escaping, creating a potential injection point into the DuckDB engine once the feature is enabled and RunCommands is implemented

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, TablesList builds a SQL command via fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL) and only escapes by doubling single quotes (strings.Replace(rawSQL, "'", "''", -1)). That is a concrete, diff-grounded construction pattern that could become a SQL injection risk depending on DuckDB string-literal parsing and how RunCommands is later implemented. However, in this diff the new sql.DB.RunCommands is stubbed to return "not implemented" and SQL expressions are effectively disabled (enableSqlExpressions always returns false), so there is no currently enabled/executable injection path shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: All DB methods (TablesList, RunCommands, QueryFramesInto) in pkg/expr/sql/db.go are unimplemented stubs returning 'not implemented', causing SQLCommand.Execute and TablesList to always fail

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces pkg/expr/sql/db.go where DB.TablesList, DB.RunCommands, and DB.QueryFramesInto all return errors.New("not implemented"). The existing code paths now call these stubs: pkg/expr/sql/parser.go changes from duck.NewInMemoryDB() to NewInMemoryDB() and then calls duckDB.RunCommands(...), which will always error; pkg/expr/sql_command.go changes to sql.NewInMemoryDB() and calls db.QueryFramesInto(...), which will always error. Therefore SQLCommand.Execute and TablesList will fail at runtime if reached.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection-prone escaping pattern: strings.Replace(rawSQL, "'", "''", -1) interpolated into fmt.Sprintf SQL instead of parameter binding, persisting in the new stub DB interface

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TablesList` still does `rawSQL = strings.Replace(rawSQL, "'", "''", -1)` and then interpolates it into `fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL)`, but because the value is placed inside a single-quoted SQL string literal and all single quotes are doubled, the diff does not demonstrate an injection break-out. Also, the newly added `DB` stub interface in `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` does not itself include this escaping/interpolation pattern; it only defines not-implemented methods.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-call NewInMemoryDB() allocation in RunCommands means no connection/engine reuse, a resource concern once the stubs are implemented

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show a per-call `NewInMemoryDB()` allocation happening inside `RunCommands()`. `RunCommands` is a method on `*DB` in `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` and currently just returns `"not implemented"` without creating a DB. While the diff does create a new in-memory DB per call site (e.g., `TablesList()` in `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` and `SQLCommand.Execute()` in `pkg/expr/sql_command.go` each call `NewInMemoryDB()`), the finding as stated misattributes this to `RunCommands` and is largely speculative about future resource reuse.

adjudication_records.issue_text: enableSqlExpressions in pkg/expr/reader.go:194-197 always returns false due to inverted/dead guard logic, permanently disabling SQL expressions regardless of feature flag

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, enableSqlExpressions() sets `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns false in both the `if enabled { ... }` branch and the final return, so it can never return true. Since ReadQuery() for QueryTypeSQL now errors when `!enabled`, SQL expressions are permanently disabled regardless of the feature flag state.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the in-memory DB implementation in pkg/expr/sql/db.go is a stub where methods return hardcoded "not implemented" errors, which aligns with the golden issue about NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands, DB.QueryFramesInto, and DB.TablesList returning such errors after removing go-duck.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TablesList in pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:23-25 now uses the stub DB's RunCommands, which always fails, breaking table-name extraction from SQL

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, TablesList now creates duckDB via NewInMemoryDB() (previously duck.NewInMemoryDB()). The new pkg/expr/sql/db.go implements NewInMemoryDB returning a *DB whose RunCommands method unconditionally returns an error ("not implemented"). Since TablesList calls duckDB.RunCommands([]string{cmd}), table-name extraction will now always fail at runtime, breaking the prior behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQLCommand.Execute in pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96-101 calls stub db.QueryFramesInto causing every runtime SQL expression query to fail

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` introduces `DB.QueryFramesInto(...)` as a stub that always returns `errors.New("not implemented")`. `SQLCommand.Execute` (pkg/expr/sql_command.go) was changed to construct `db := sql.NewInMemoryDB()` and then call `db.QueryFramesInto(...)`, so any execution reaching this code path will deterministically error and fail SQL expression evaluation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of github.com/scottlepp/go-duck from go.mod may break other importers not touched in the diff, requiring a full-repo grep before merging

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck` imports were removed in the touched files (`pkg/expr/sql/parser.go`, `pkg/expr/sql_command.go`) alongside removing the module from `go.mod`. Whether other files still import `go-duck` cannot be verified from this diff alone, so the claim that removal "may break other importers not touched" is not diff-verifiable and is essentially a generic precaution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: go.sum/go.work.sum churn suggests transitive dependency graph may have been hand-edited, risking checksum verification failures in non-workspace builds

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows typical Go module/workspace maintenance: several deps are removed from root go.mod and corresponding entries are removed from go.sum, while some checksums are added to go.work.sum (workspace-wide sums). This pattern can result from `go mod tidy` / `go work sync` and does not, by itself, verify that files were hand-edited or that non-workspace builds will fail checksum verification. The diff provides no concrete evidence of a checksum mismatch or verification failure scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TablesList retains DuckDB-specific json_serialize_sql SQL against the stub DB, leaking abstraction details into the caller

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, TablesList still builds and executes the DuckDB-specific command `SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')` via `duckDB.RunCommands(...)` after switching from `duck.NewInMemoryDB()` to `NewInMemoryDB()`. But the new pkg/expr/sql/db.go stub DB’s `RunCommands` always returns `errors.New("not implemented")`, so TablesList is now guaranteed to fail at runtime, and it also hard-codes DuckDB-specific SQL despite the new generic-looking DB abstraction.
